Article Title: 100% tariffs for India? US Senate advances key Russian sanctions bill
Article Text:
India could face 100% if Russia Sanctions Bill becomes a law

The US Senate on Tuesday overwhelmingly advanced a bipartisan bill that would give President Donald Trump sweeping powers to impose new sanctions on Russia and penalise major buyers of its energy exports, including India and China.The legislation would allow the president to impose a 500 per cent tariff on Russian goods imported into the US and an additional 100 per cent tariff on the world's five largest buyers of Russian crude oil and natural gas, as well as the top five countries found to be helping Moscow evade energy sanctions. India and China are among Russia's biggest energy customers.The Senate voted 86-12 to clear the first procedural hurdle for the bill, which was championed by the late Republican Senator Lindsey Graham. The measure could pass the Senate later this week, although it is unlikely to become law before September because the House has already begun its August recess.The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031, preserving US authority to impose secondary sanctions on non-US companies doing business with Iran. It includes broader measures targeting Russian oil and gas exports while allowing the president to waive sanctions if deemed to be in the US national interest.Read also - Reverse oil flow: India supplies gasoline to Russia - why it matters President Donald Trump has signalled support for the legislation. Earlier on Tuesday, he met Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy at the White House before Zelenskyy travelled to Capitol Hill, where he urged lawmakers to maintain sanctions pressure on Moscow."Sanctions pressure on Russia is very important," Zelenskyy said. "It's not only about your money. It's also a big signal to Europe, a big signal to Ukraine."Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer said the bill would send a strong message to Russian President Vladimir Putin, while some Democrats warned that the measure could also significantly expand Trump's tariff powers.If enacted, the legislation would mark one of the strongest US efforts yet to curb Russia's energy revenues and could have significant implications for India, which has sharply increased purchases of discounted Russian crude since the Ukraine war began.
Article Summary: The US Senate on Tuesday overwhelmingly advanced a bipartisan bill that would give President Donald Trump sweeping powers to impose new sanctions on Russia. The legislation would allow the president to impose a 500 per cent tariff on Russian goods imported into the US. The bill also extends the Iran Sanctions Act of 1996 through 2031, preserving US authority to impose secondary sanctions on non-US companies.

Article Title: Crude prices climb over 4% as renewed Middle East tensions, inventory draw fuel supply fears
Article Text: Oil prices rebounded sharply on Wednesday, reversing part of the previous session's steep decline, as renewed tensions in the Middle East reignited concerns over global crude supplies. Lower US crude inventories and expectations around OPEC+ production policy also lent support to the market.Brent crude climbed 4.41% to $87.80 a barrel, gaining $3.71, while US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 4.23%, or $3.35, to $82.61 a barrel.The market had retreated nearly 5% on Tuesday, touching a two-week low after hopes emerged that the pause in hostilities between Washington and Tehran could pave the way for renewed diplomatic engagement. Those expectations were tempered as the regional security situation deteriorated once again.Fresh concerns centred on the Strait of Hormuz, a key oil shipping route. Any prolonged disruption in the waterway could raise energy costs further, increase transportation expenses, push fuel prices higher and add inflationary pressure across major economies.Military developments in the region also remained in focus.Saudi Arabia said that it had joined the US Central Command (CENTCOM) in carrying out air strikes on Iran-backed militant targets in Iraq after recent drone attacks on Saudi oil facilities. The Saudi defence ministry said that the kingdom was not seeking escalation but would respond to actions threatening its security and critical infrastructure.CENTCOM said the joint operation targeted multiple Iran-aligned militant logistics and weapons sites in eastern Iraq on July 28 after more than 30 IRGC-directed drone attacks were launched over the previous 72 hours against US forces and Saudi energy infrastructure.At the same time, signs of tighter US crude supplies added to bullish sentiment. Market sources, citing data from the American Petroleum Institute, said US crude inventories fell by around 3.3 million barrels in the week ended July 24. Gasoline stocks, however, increased by 918,000 barrels, while distillate inventories rose by 355,000 barrels from the previous week. Official data from the Energy Information Administration is due later on Wednesday.The rising tensions have also prompted shipping companies operating in the Gulf to remain on alert. Several operators have altered sailing routes, tightened onboard security measures and reassessed insurance coverage amid fears of further attacks on commercial vessels.Oil prices also found support from expectations that OPEC+ could pause planned production increases for three months from October after completing the scheduled return of barrels following voluntary output cuts.The market has remained highly volatile amid the US-Israeli war in Iran, which has disrupted global crude flows, particularly following the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz.US President Donald Trump, who called off a two-week US bombing campaign over the weekend, told Fox News on Tuesday that there were "good talks" with Iran, while warning that more strikes could follow if negotiations fail. Iran, however, denied that it is seeking to resume talks with the United States.
Article Summary: Brent crude climbed 4.41% to $87.80 a barrel, gaining $3.71. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude rose 4.23%, or £3.35, to $82.61 a barrel. The market had retreated nearly 5% on Tuesday, touching a two-week low.

Article Title: Rupee gains for fourth straight session as dollar weakens, oil prices remain below $90
Article Text: Rupee extended its rally for the fourth consecutive session on Wednesday, gaining 5 paise to trade at 95.77 against the US dollar, supported by a softer dollar and lower crude oil prices.The currency also drew strength from improved sentiment in domestic equities, with foreign institutional investors turning buyers in Indian stocks, forex traders said.At the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee started the session at 95.70 against the US dollar and later traded at 95.77, marking a 5 paise rise from its previous closing level.The currency had ended Tuesday’s session at 95.82 per dollar, gaining 17 paise during the day. This followed a 74 paise rise over the previous two trading sessions.Market participants tracked movements in the dollar index, which was down 0.12% at 101.14. The index was under pressure ahead of the Federal Reserve’s monetary policy announcements.Crude oil prices also remained in focus. Brent crude futures, the global oil benchmark, rose 4.27% but continued to trade lower at $87.68 per barrel.According to analysts, crude oil prices moved higher overnight after hopes of a return to negotiations and a ceasefire between the US and Iran were hit following the US military’s statement that Iran had launched multiple ballistic missiles at American forces on Tuesday.US Central Command said all Iranian missiles were successfully intercepted and added that US forces "remain vigilant and at a high state of readiness."Meanwhile, gains in domestic equities supported the rupee’s movement. The Sensex advanced 682.57 points, or 0.89%, to 77,448.49, while the Nifty rose 186.85 points, or 0.78%, to 24,172.20.Foreign Institutional Investors bought Indian equities worth Rs 755.33 crore on a net basis on Tuesday, according to exchange data.
Article Summary: Rupee extended its rally for the fourth consecutive session on Wednesday, gaining 5 paise to trade at 95.77 against the US dollar. The currency also drew strength from improved sentiment in domestic equities, with foreign institutional investors turning buyers in Indian stocks.

Gold ended last week with a modest gain of nearly 0.9%, but the recovery looked more like a technical bounce than a change in the underlying trend. A sharp pullback in crude oil prices from above $100 per barrel and easing US Treasury yields offered some relief to bullion. However, the broader picture remained cautious, with gold continuing to trade within a five-week consolidation range as markets preferred to wait for fresh macro triggers rather than chase prices higher.Encouragingly, the World Gold Council reported 18.1 tonnes of net ETF inflows for the week ended July 24, putting July on track to become the first month in three with positive inflows, suggesting investor sentiment is beginning to stabilize despite recent weakness.This week, gold has once again traded cautiously, slipping lower as markets avoided taking aggressive positions ahead of today's Federal Reserve policy decision.At the same time, one encouraging development has been gold's ability to repeatedly hold around the $4,000/oz mark. Despite higher rate expectations and a stronger US dollar, physical holdings have remained broadly stable near 4,000 tonnes, indicating that long-term buyers continue to accumulate at lower levels even as speculative demand has cooled.The spotlight this week is firmly on today's FOMC policy decision, which is expected to set the tone for gold's next major move. While markets still assign the highest probability to the Fed leaving rates unchanged, expectations of a future rate hike have increased notably, making Chair Warsh's comments on inflation and the September policy path even more important.Beyond the Fed, traders will closely watch US GDP, Core PCE inflation, and the Employment Cost Index, as these releases will shape expectations for future interest rate decisions. A hawkish message that reinforces higher-for-longer interest rates could strengthen the US dollar and bond yields, putting renewed pressure on gold. Conversely, if the Fed adopts a more balanced tone and upcoming inflation data shows signs of easing, bullion could extend its recovery from the $4,000/oz support area.Spot gold support is seen at $3,960 and $3,860, while resistance is placed at $4,220 and $4,300. For MCX Gold, the strong support zone remains at Rs 1,38,000-Rs 1,39,000, with Rs 1,47,000 acting as the immediate resistance. Overall, the medium-term bias remains constructive as long as physical demand continues to absorb selling pressure near the $4,000 level, but the Fed's guidance today will be crucial in determining the next directional move.Silver, too, has been consolidating at lower levels, trading in a narrow $55–62/oz range since late June. For now, prices are largely taking cues from Fed policy expectations and the direction of the US dollar, while the ongoing supply deficit continues to provide a supportive medium-term outlook.

Article Title: Delhi high court orders winding up of Paytm Payments Bank
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Delhi high court has ordered the winding up of Paytm Payments Bank, weeks after RBI cancelled its banking licence citing concerns over its operations and management.The court, through orders dated July 8 and July 22, 2026, directed that Paytm Payments Bank be wound up under provisions of the Banking Regulation Act, 1949, read with the Companies Act, 2013.It also appointed Girikumar M Nair, former chief general manager of State Bank of India, as the official liquidator. RBI had on April 24 cancelled the bank's licence with immediate effect.
Article Summary: Delhi high court has ordered the winding up of Paytm Payments Bank. RBI had on April 24 cancelled the bank's licence with immediate effect. The court has appointed Girikumar M Nair, former chief general manager of State Bank of India as the official liquidator.

Article Title: 'Transformation of Air India may take up to a decade'
Article Text:
File photo: Air India

NEW DELHI: Air India's transformation to a world class airline, following its return to founder Tata Group in 2022, could take up to a decade due to serious headwinds the aviation industry and the Maharaja have encountered in recent years.The earlier assessment of giving the airline a facelift in five years under Vihaan programme has proven to be a grossly optimistic one, requiring a reset of timelines."Given where it began, AI's transformation must be seen as a five- to 10-year journey, considering years-long supply chain disruptions in key components, need to overhaul legacy systems, culture and fleet, and creation of a large cadre of technical and airline professionals," Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran said.He pointed to issues AI has faced that have caused timeline overrun. "Few businesses are as vulnerable to war and fuel pressures as aviation. This year, Air India faced three headwinds. Airspace closures, West Asia conflict-driven fuel price hikes and foreign exchange fluctuations. Crash of AI 171 made it the most challenging year for Air India."
Article Summary: The earlier assessment of giving the airline a facelift in five years under Vihaan programme has proven to be a grossly optimistic one, requiring a reset of timelines. "Few businesses are as vulnerable to war and fuel pressures as aviation," Tata Sons chairman N Chandrasekaran said.

Article Title: Priceless stake: Noel's children now Tata Sons shareholders
Article Text:
File photo: Noel Tata

MUMBAI: Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata's three children have become shareholders of Tata Sons for the first time, according to the company's FY26 documents, after inheriting shares from their grandmother Simone Tata.Leah, Maya and Neville Tata - all of whom work within the Tata Group - now hold two Tata Sons shares each. The stakes are modest in number, but not in value: a single Tata Sons share is estimated to be worth Rs 4-5 crore. The FY25 documents showed Simone holding eight Tata Sons shares.She died in Dec 2025, and her holding was split equally among her son and grandchildren. Noel's stake rose to 4,060 shares from 4,058, while Leah, Maya and Neville were added as shareholders with two shares each.Noel's older half-brother Jimmy Tata holds 3,262 Tata Sons shares. Ratan Tata, who died in Oct 2024, continues to be listed as holder of 3,368 shares - he had bequeathed them to his two philanthropic foundations, but the transfer is yet to go through.Tata Sons' other individual shareholders include Shapoor Mistry, Noel's brother-in-law (54 shares); his nephews Firoz and Zahan Mistry (27 shares each); Piloo Tata, widow of Minocher Tata - a grand-nephew of Group founder Jamsetji Tata (487 shares); her children Jimmy Tata and Vera Choksey (157 shares each); and Aishwarya, Bhavani and Jay Pratapsingh Chauhan of the royal family of Chhota Udaipur, Gujarat (one share).Almost all of them acquired their holdings through inheritance - Tata Sons, it may be noted, has not altered its equity capital in decades.
Article Summary: Leah, Maya and Neville Tata - all of whom work within the Tata Group - now hold two Tata Sons shares each. The stakes are modest in number, but not in value: a single Tata Sons share is estimated to be worth Rs 4-5 crore.

Article Title: Bad debt of PSBs at lowest levels in many decades: Government
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Government on Tuesday said that public sector banks are in good financial health, reporting significant improvement in balance sheets , high levels of profits and bad debt at lowest levels in several decades."Further, public sector banks have recorded sustained credit growth across different sectors of the economy," minister of state for finance Pankaj Chaudhary told Rajya Sabha. The state-run lenders reported cumulative profits of just under Rs 2 lakh crore during the last financial year, nearly three times the level of Rs 67,000 crore seen in 2021-22. Over the last five years, gross non-performing assets or the stock of bad debt has fallen from 7.3% of advances to 1.9%, government told Parliament.While government had infused capital in these banks to help them tide over the massive pile of bad debt, some of which was not recognised in their books, steps such as the Insolvency & Bankruptcy Code also helped in the clean up drive. Besides, higher economic activity has helped accelerate credit flow across the economy, with steps such as the Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme, first used after the Covid lockdown, helping insulate banks in times of crisis.Even after West Asia war, government has introduced ECLGS 5.0 to help businesses deal with liquidity mismatches to support credit flow of up to Rs 2,55,000 crore.In response to a question on Monday, the junior minister for finance had told the Lok Sabha that so far, guarantees have been issued for Rs 1.9 lakh crore with some of the sectors dominated by small businesses such as trading, food processing, textiles topping the list.While civil aviation is also eligible for benefits up to Rs 5,000 crore, so far, eight guarantees of Rs 163 crore have been issued.
Article Summary: State-run lenders reported cumulative profits of just under Rs 2 lakh crore during the last financial year. Over the last five years, gross non-performing assets or the stock of bad debt has fallen from 7.3% of advances to 1.9%.

Article Title: As inflation bites, HUL to take more price hikes
Article Text:
Representative image

MUMBAI: Hindustan Unilever (HUL) will take more price increases in the coming months as shaky peace prospects in West Asia continue to keep commodity costs volatile, the consumer goods giant said on Tuesday.It projected inflation to stay in the range of 2-5% in the Sept quarter. The maker of Dove shampoos and Knorr soups said that demand for soaps, detergents, packaged food and other household staples was stable in the June quarter, pushing growth to a 13-quarter high even though inflation worries weighed on investor sentiment, dragging HUL's stock price down by nearly 7%---the biggest one-day fall since March 2020, according to Bloomberg estimates."Overall, we see that the situation continues to remain volatile. Between Sept quarter versus June quarter, we see a sequential inflation, which could range between 2-5%. So, we will continue to take calibrated pricing into the quarter, depending on how inflation pans out," MD & CEO Priya Nair said in a post-earnings briefing, maintaining that FY27 will be better than FY26.Nair, who will complete a year at the corner office on Aug 1, said that HUL will chase volume-led revenue growth and a wide portfolio spanning categories and price packs somewhat shields it against periods of economic volatility.HUL took a 5% price hike in the June quarter.HUL's revenue from operations increased by 10% to Rs 17,341 crore on a consolidated basis in Q1FY27. Net profits declined to Rs 2,680 crore in Q1 from Rs 2,768 crore in the year-ago period, recording a 3.2% dip due to a one-off tax credit in Q1FY26.The company reported an underlying volume growth (UVG) of 5% and an underlying sales growth (USG) of 10% during the quarter, which HUL said was driven equally by volume and price."This growth has come at the cost of stressed margins year-on-year, especially in home care and personal care categories which has led to markets reacting negatively," said independent consultant Akshay Dsouza, adding that an inflationary environment is leading to continued stress on margins.HUL's stock price ended lower at Rs 2,023.1 apiece on the BSE on Tuesday.The war-led disruption of energy supplies pushed up prices of crude oil, nudging FMCG companies to take at least one round of price hikes. Crude oil has a direct bearing on packaging and logistics costs.Besides, crude derivatives are used to manufacture a range of household products including lotions, detergents and dish-washing liquids. HUL said that it remains watchful of the impact of El Nino on monsoons. Agriculture currently accounts for about 15% of India's GDP and the overall impact of monsoons could be around 50-60 bps to GDP, Nair said, adding that progression and geographical spread of the rains will be key.
Article Summary: Consumer goods giant projected inflation to stay in the range of 2-5% in the Sept quarter. Demand for soaps, detergents, packaged food and other household staples was stable in the June quarter. HUL's stock price ended lower at Rs 2,023.1 apiece on the BSE on Tuesday.

Article Title: Industrial output grows 7.3% in June, fastest in 22 months
Article Text:
File photo

NEW DELHI: Industrial production grew 7.3% in June, a 22-month high, as against 2.2% a year ago on account of strong expansion in manufacturing, electricity and gas supply in the month, due to low base effect and resilient domestic demand conditions in the face of prolonged crisis in West Asia and erratic monsoon. Sequentially too, industrial production fared better in June as compared with the downwardly revised figure of 5% in May.The index of industrial production (IIP) data released by the statistics ministry Tuesday pegged the first quarter (April-June) IIP growth at 5.8% as against 3.4% a year ago.Among the sub sectors -- electricity and gas supply (10.6%) recorded the highest growth during the month on account of sustained heat wave conditions. The manufacturing sector, which has a weight of 76% in the index, grew 7.8%, followed by water supply, sewerage & waste management (6.1%) and mining and quarrying (1%).Dipti Deshpande, principal economist at Crisil said Indian firms have "adroitly sourced" materials from alternative markets and used domestic inventories to sail past the supply straitjackets of the conflict, with strong domestic demand and sustained retail credit growth also providing an offset to geopolitical uncertainties.Among the manufacturing sector, 19 out of 23 industries recorded growth in June, with electrical equipment industry having the highest growth (34%). Sectors like motor vehicles, trailers and semi-trailers (17.5%), textiles (13.7%), beverages (12.5%) and food products (10.8%) also showed robust growth.CareEdge Ratings chief economist Rajani Sinha said high input prices due to uncertain global environment will continue to pose risk for the industrial sector, along with an erratic monsoon, particularly its impact on kharif production and rural demand.India Ratings director Megha Arora expects IIP growth to moderate 5.4% in July on account of adverse base effect. Deshpande added that a slowing global growth is weakening export demand and elevated input costs and price pass throughs are expected to squeeze producer margins, temper consumption demand and moderate industrial output in coming months.
Article Summary: Industrial production grew 7.3% in June, a 22-month high, as against 2.2% a year ago. Strong expansion in manufacturing, electricity and gas supply in the month. Sequentially too, industrial production fared better in June as compared with the downwardly revised figure of 5% in May.

Article Title: For ease of liquidity & business, government to amend MSME Act
Article Text:
The Union Cabinet has approved amendments to the MSME Development Act to improve liquidity, strengthen the Udyam portal, decriminalise minor offences, and speed up payment resolution for small businesses. (Representative image)

NEW DELHI: Small businesses supplying goods and services to central public sector undertakings (CPSUs) will get their dues cleared faster under proposed amendments to the MSME Development Act, 2006, introduced in Parliament Tuesday, that seek mandatory digital invoicing, stronger protection against delayed payments and faster settlement of disputes.The move is aimed at improving liquidity and reducing the long waiting period that often leaves small businesses short of working capital despite having completed their supplies or services.The Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development (Amendment) Bill, 2026, seeks to update the Act of 2006 by simplifying registration and compliance, strengthening payment-related safeguards and decriminalising certain offences. Under the proposed changes to the law, all invoices raised by MSMEs on CPSUs will have to be routed through TReDS - an electronic platform that helps small businesses turn unpaid customer invoices into immediate cash.State governments may impose a similar requirement for invoices raised by MSMEs on their public sector undertakings. To speed up resolution of payment disputes, states will be required to establish additional micro and small enterprise facilitation councils.The councils will have 3-5 members, with the inclusion of a legal expert becoming mandatory.The bill also proposes a free national digital registration platform for MSMEs. The common platform is intended to simplify registration and make it easier for businesses to access govt schemes, incentives and institutional support. A significant provision deals with appeals against awards passed in favour of MSMEs. A buyer challenging an award may be required to release at least 50% of the awarded amount if the case remains pending for more than six months.Courts will also be empowered to order payments to an MSME from the amount deposited by the buyer during the appeal.
Article Summary: The move is aimed at improving liquidity and reducing the long waiting period that often leaves small businesses short of working capital. Under the proposed changes to the law, all invoices raised by MSMEs on CPSUs will have to be routed through TReDS. A significant provision deals with appeals against awards passed in favour of small businesses.

Article Title: MCC new rules for NEET UG 2026 counselling: Upgrade seats, resignation and NRI quota updates
Article Text:
NEET UG 2026 counselling new rules: MCC introduces online resignation, no reporting for upgrades

NEET UG 2026 counselling

:

No physical reporting required for candidates seeking upgrades



Seat resignation facility moved online



NRI quota applicants can upload documents online



MCC conducts training for states and medical colleges



Information on seats and fees to support choices



Key MCC counselling changes at a glance



New update

Details

No physical reporting for upgrades

Candidates choosing upgradation need not report to colleges only for admission formalities

Online seat resignation

Eligible candidates can resign through the MCC portal within deadlines

NRI document upload

NRI quota applicants for deemed universities can upload documents online

Stakeholder training

MCC conducting sessions for state authorities and medical institutions

Seat and fee information

Authorities asked to provide details for informed choices



The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has introduced major changes in the online counselling process for NEET UG and postgraduate medical admissions from the current academic session. The new measures aim to simplify admission procedures, reduce physical paperwork and make the counselling system more transparent for medical aspirants.The updates were communicated by the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare to state counselling authorities ahead of the NEET UG 2026 counselling process. The Karnataka Examination Authority (KEA) also informed candidates that MCC will begin counselling shortly and highlighted the key changes introduced in the system.Under the revised counselling process, candidates who receive a seat allotment and select the “Upgrade” or “Willing to Upgrade” option in subsequent rounds will no longer need to physically report to the allotted college only for completing admission formalities.Their allotted seat will remain protected in the counselling system while they participate in further rounds, subject to the existing MCC counselling rules.The change is expected to reduce unnecessary travel and paperwork for candidates waiting for better seat options.MCC has introduced an online resignation facility for candidates who wish to leave their allotted seats, wherever resignation is permitted under counselling guidelines.Candidates will now be able to submit resignation requests through the MCC counselling portal within the specified deadline. They will not be required to visit the allotted medical college physically for submitting resignation documents.The facility will be available only according to the applicable rules and timelines announced for each counselling phase.Candidates seeking NRI reservation benefits in deemed universities will now be able to upload their required documents directly through the MCC counselling portal.Earlier, document submission procedures for NRI quota applications involved additional coordination. The new online facility has been introduced to make the verification process more accessible and organised for applicants.To ensure smooth implementation of the updated counselling system, MCC has started orientation and training programmes for stakeholders involved in medical admissions.Training sessions were conducted for State Directorate of Medical Education authorities in May and June 2026. A separate training session for medical institutions was organised on July 27, 2026, with additional sessions planned for government and private medical colleges.MCC has also highlighted the importance of providing candidates with clear information about available seats and institutional fee structures.MCC conducts counselling for 15% All India Quota (AIQ) seats and 100% seats in deemed and central universities under NEET UG. Since most medical seats are managed by respective states and Union Territories, authorities have been asked to ensure that details regarding seats and fees are easily available to candidates.Candidates preparing for NEET UG 2026 counselling should follow official MCC notifications and keep required documents ready before registration and choice-filling stages begin.
Article Summary: The Medical Counselling Committee (MCC) has introduced major changes in the online counselling process for NEET UG and postgraduate medical admissions from the current academic session. The new measures aim to simplify admission procedures, reduce physical paperwork and make the counselling system more transparent for medical aspirants.

Article Title: Is Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah finally joining WWE? Here's what we know so far
Article Text:
Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah. Image via: WWE

Will Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah step into the ring?

What Aalyah's WWE history looks like so far

Who is Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah?

Aalyah Mysterio appears to be closing in on a WWE career of her own, with training reports and a string of social media posts pointing toward a full-time move to Orlando. Rey Mysterio's daughter has spent the better part of two years working out at WWE's developmental home, and the signs of a formal arrival keep piling up.None of it is official yet. WWE has not announced a signing, but the pattern, from tryouts to specialized camps to a cake that all but spelled it out, tells its own story.The clearest signal came from Aalyah herself. She recently posted photos of a cake designed to look like her in wrestling gear, topped with a mask styled after her father's, and iced with the phrase "Florida's about to get 619'D." Paired with report that she's expected to train at the Performance Center more regularly, the message reads as a near-confirmation that a full-time move to Orlando is coming, even without a press release to back it up.The training itself has been building for a while. Aalyah went through initial tryouts at the Performance Center in 2025 after finishing her degree at UC San Diego, then returned this February for a more demanding two-week stretch, training Monday through Friday. Rey Mysterio has said she enjoyed that stretch of work and is now focused on training going forward.She's also sought out instruction outside WWE's own building.Aalyah has trained at Nattie Neidhart and TJ Wilson's Dungeon facility, and she attended Bayley's Lodestone camp during WrestleMania 42 week in Las Vegas, a women's wrestling program that also drew Sherilyn Guerrero, daughter of Eddie Guerrero, and Jazzy Yang, daughter of Jimmy Wang Yang.Aalyah isn't a stranger to WWE television. She appeared regularly during the 2020 feud pitting Rey and Dominik Mysterio against Seth Rollins and Buddy Murphy, where she was written into a romantic storyline opposite Murphy. She resurfaced briefly in 2023 during the build to the Mysterio family's WrestleMania 39 program, and she'd already made a cameo as a child during a 2010 segment, giving her a longer on-screen history with the company than most prospective signees.Rey Mysterio has spoken before about backing his daughter if she chose wrestling. He said Angie once asked what he'd do if Aalyah wanted to get in the ring, and his answer was direct: he'd train her himself, the way he did with Dominik, and support her fully.Aalyah Gutiérrez was born on August 20, 2001, the second child of Rey Mysterio and Angie Gutiérrez. She grew up around WWE storylines built around her family, most notably the Mysterio-Rollins-Murphy program, and she's carried the Mysterio name into her own developmental run now. Academically, her path has run through UC San Diego, though the record on her exact course of study varies across reports, one describing a completed human biology degree, another citing an acceptance into UC San Diego's medical school. That detail remains unresolved pending further confirmation.What isn't in question is the direction she's heading. Between the Performance Center reps, the Dungeon sessions, and a cake that did most of the talking for her, Aalyah Mysterio looks like a signing WWE simply hasn't announced yet. The next marker to watch is whether that changes on NXT programming, and how soon.
Article Summary: Rey Mysterio's daughter Aalyah has spent the better part of two years working out at WWE's developmental home. She recently posted photos of a cake designed to look like her in wrestling gear. The message reads as a near-confirmation that a full-time move to Orlando is coming.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay's new office: Inside sea-facing CMO replacing Fort St George
Article Text:
Namakkal Kavignar Maaligai at Secretariat, Fort St. George in Chennai.

New office plan





CHENNAI: It is official. Chief minister C Joseph Vijay will move out of the cramped confines of Fort St George and check into a plush sea-facing 11-storey Namakkal Kavignar Maligai on the state secretariat campus.The VVIP floor was being readied for infrastructure, security and landscaping overhaul when TOI visited the site on Tuesday.The entire chief minister’s office (CMO) will function from the 10th floor of the building, placing Vijay directly above the offices of senior secretaries to enable faster coordination and easier access for meetings.The public works department (PWD) has cordoned off nearly half of the 10th floor, including the sprawling 5,000+ sqft conference hall, while four police personnel have been posted to secure the corridor leading to the proposed office.“The conference hall, where the finance minister recently presented the white paper, will be converted into the CMO. It will include the CM’s main office, a spacious meeting hall for visiting dignitaries, an ante-room for the chief minister to rest, and a dining area,” said an official with the public dept’s govt estate wing, which is involved in the planning.The office space was evacuated on Tuesday, and PWD’s engineering and construction wing will float an open tender soon for designing and developing the new office, officials said.The makeover extends beyond the building. The public dept has directed the PWD to clear encroachments along the historic Fort wall, where old wooden furniture from various govt offices was stacked.It has requested the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI) to hand over a portion of the King’s Barracks so the frontage can be redeveloped into additional parking space. The entire area surrounding Namakkal Kavignar Maligai will also be cleaned, landscaped and beautified.Officials said shifting the CMO to Namakkal Kavignar Maligai would significantly improve administrative efficiency, as nearly 30 depts already function from the building.“It is much easier to conduct meetings if the CM is in the same building. Shifting files will also become easier. Besides, the top floor has ample lighting, ventilation and space, unlike Fort St George. The building also allows quicker evacuation or rescue during emergencies,” a senior secretary said.Traffic police officials at the secretariat said only four categories of vehicles — the CM’s car, ambulance, police vehicles and fire engines — will be permitted to stop in front of the building.A proposal to develop the state govt canteen near the building has been sent. The canteen has a damaged roof, poor air circulation, and inadequate fans, besides unhygienic conditions.“The CM vehicle will be parked in the front. He will enter through the secretariat gate, take a right in front of the Assembly, and proceed directly to Namakkal Kavignar Maligai. All obstructions along the route will be removed,” a traffic police officer said.Around 6,000 employees now work from the secretariat building. The PWD has asked police to streamline parking by preventing two and three-layer bike parking on the premises and shifting excess motorcycles to the open ground outside.On Tuesday, however, operations remained largely unchanged, with consultants, architects, NGOs and members of the public continuing to access the building as usual without any check.“Once the CM shifts here, security screening will become much tighter,” a police personnel posted at the building’s reception said.
Article Summary: Chief minister C Joseph Vijay will move out of the cramped confines of Fort St George and check into a plush sea-facing 11-storey Namakkal Kavignar Maligai. The entire chief minister’s office (CMO) will function from the 10th floor of the building.

Article Title: US stock market today: S&P 500, Dow Jones trade flat; Nasdaq drops over 1% as chips stocks drop
Article Text:
Lofty expectations have placed particular pressure on semiconductor companies and other firms that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom.

US stock market today: Most Wall Street indices traded higher on Tuesday, although semiconductor stocks continued to face heavy selling across global markets. Oil prices also extended their decline after retreating from the two-month highs reached last week.In early trading, the S&P 500 was little changed, masking significant divergence across sectors. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 385 points, or 0.7%, while the Nasdaq Composite slipped over 1%, according to an AP report.Broader market sentiment remained supported by another round of stronger-than-expected corporate earnings. Coca-Cola advanced 5.8% after reporting a 7% increase in revenue, despite what Chief Executive Officer Henrique Braun described as “a dynamic consumer landscape.”Sherwin-Williams climbed 7% and Illinois Tool Works added 3.7% after both companies posted quarterly profits that exceeded analysts' expectations. Over the longer term, stock prices tend to track corporate earnings, and expectations have remained elevated as US equities continue to trade close to record highs.Those lofty expectations have placed particular pressure on semiconductor companies and other firms that have been among the biggest beneficiaries of the artificial intelligence boom.Micron Technology, for instance, has seen its share price more than triple this year following exceptionally strong growth. During the quarter ended May 28, the company reported revenue that was more than four times higher than a year earlier.However, investors are increasingly questioning whether such rapid expansion can be sustained. Concerns have emerged that major spending on memory chips could slow if artificial intelligence fails to deliver the expected gains in profitability or productivity. At the same time, lower-cost AI models emerging from China could reduce demand for memory chips and conventional computing power.Micron's shares fell 8.4%, making it the biggest drag on the S&P 500. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) declined 7.7%, while Nvidia lost 1.1%, adding to the weakness in the technology sector.The selloff was even more pronounced in overseas markets earlier in the day. Sharp declines in SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics pulled South Korea's KOSPI index down 10.8%, with losses severe enough to trigger temporary trading halts in Seoul.“We believe the market was likely spooked by the progress of China’s chipmaking equipment capabilities, and was worried that this progress would threaten the competitive position of global chipmaking and chip equipment leaders,” said equity analyst Jing Jie Yu of Morningstar.“That said, we believe the sell-off today is largely a knee-jerk reaction and overdone,” he said, adding that the leadership position of the world's major chipmakers is unlikely to face any meaningful threat.In the commodities market, Brent crude for October delivery fell 2.2% to $83.97 a barrel. Just last week, the September contract had briefly surged to as high as $102 per barrel amid concerns that the conflict in the Middle East could disrupt global crude supplies.The decline in oil prices also supported the bond market. The yield on the benchmark 10-year US Treasury note eased to 4.62% from 4.65% at Monday's close.
Article Summary: Most Wall Street indices traded higher on Tuesday, although semiconductor stocks continued to face heavy selling across global markets. Oil prices also extended their decline after retreating from the two-month highs reached last week. Broader market sentiment remained supported by another round of stronger-than- expected corporate earnings.

Article Title: Boeing posts bigger-than-expected Q2 loss as Air Force One costs rise by $280 million
Article Text:
A Boeing 737 MAX aircraft. (AP Photo)

Air Force One programme hits Boeing earnings

Cash flow improves despite losses

Trump’s temporary Air Force One aircraft

FAA flags seat installation issue on 737 MAX jets

Boeing reported a larger-than-expected second-quarter loss on Tuesday as higher costs linked to the delayed Air Force One replacement programme weighed on its results.The US planemaker, however, reported positive free cash flow and maintained its annual guidance as it works to stabilise operations and increase aircraft production.According to news agency Reuters, Boeing took a $280 million charge on the Air Force One replacement programme due to higher engineering costs needed to complete two delayed presidential aircraft by 2028.The charge contributed to a net loss of $428 million in the second quarter.The company reported an adjusted loss of 76 cents per share, wider than analysts' expectation of a 30-cent loss per share, according to LSEG data.However, the loss was narrower compared with the $1.24 per share loss reported in the same quarter last year.The two 747-8 aircraft, being developed under a $3.9 billion fixed-price contract signed in 2018, are now around four years behind schedule and more than $1 billion over budget.Despite the quarterly setback, Boeing generated $631 million in free cash flow, compared with a negative $200 million during the same period last year.The company said the improvement was partly driven by higher-than-expected customer payments.Boeing retained its full-year free cash flow forecast of $1 billion to $3 billion, which would mark its first positive annual cash flow result since 2023. The company is also increasing production of its best-selling 737 MAX narrow-body jets as part of its recovery efforts.Capital spending rose during the quarter, mainly due to expansion of 787 production capabilities in South Carolina and military aircraft production facilities in the St Louis, Missouri, region.Meanwhile, US President Donald Trump has been using a Qatari-donated 747-8 aircraft as a temporary Air Force One replacement. Trump said the aircraft would soon be sent for upgrades after concerns were raised over its security features.In a separate development, the US Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has proposed a directive requiring checks and fixes on hundreds of Boeing 737 MAX jets registered in the US after finding that some passenger seats may have been incorrectly installed.The FAA said the issue could cause seats to detach during an emergency landing or block aisles, potentially slowing evacuation and posing risks to passengers and crew members.The proposed directive applies to 453 aircraft registered in the US. The agency said each affected seat assembly could take about one working hour to fix, with no replacement parts required.Boeing said it had issued guidance to operators about the issue in December 2025 and supported the FAA making the guidance mandatory.
Article Summary: Boeing took a $280 million charge on the Air Force One replacement programme due to higher engineering costs needed to complete two delayed presidential aircraft by 2028. The two 747-8 aircraft are now around four years behind schedule and more than $1 billion over budget. But Boeing generated $631 million in free cash flow, compared with a negative $200 million during the same period last year.

Article Title: South Korea's KOSPI crashes around 11%: Circuit breaker triggered, market sees worst session in 5 months
Article Text:
So far this month, the KOSPI has fallen 29%, surpassing its previous record monthly decline of 27% recorded in October 1997.

South Korean equities suffered their steepest one-day decline in nearly five months on Tuesday, with the benchmark KOSPI sliding almost 11% as a global rout in semiconductor stocks battered SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Investor concerns were further amplified by the blockbuster stock market debut of China's CXMT, which intensified fears over rising competition from Chinese chipmakers.The KOSPI ended the session down 732.09 points, or 10.84%, at 6,023.66, marking its biggest daily fall since March 4, when the index recorded a historic decline following the outbreak of the Iran war, according to a Reuters report.During intraday trade, the index dropped as much as 11.3%, triggering a circuit breaker for the eighth time this year and the 14th time on record. It also slipped below the 6,000 mark for the first time since April 14.So far this month, the KOSPI has fallen 29%, surpassing its previous record monthly decline of 27% recorded in October 1997. Despite being down 34% from its June peak of 9,114.55, the index remains 43% higher on a year-to-date basis.Memory chip manufacturer SK Hynix plunged 14.7% after its American depositary receipts (ADRs) fell to an all-time low in New York and dropped below their original US listing price.Samsung Electronics, another heavyweight constituent of the index, declined 14.4%, marking its sharpest single-day fall since October 2008.Together, SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics account for more than half of the KOSPI's total weighting, magnifying the impact of the semiconductor selloff on the broader market. Both companies are scheduled to announce their second-quarter earnings later this week.Investor sentiment was also weighed down by developments in China, including the blockbuster listing of ChangXin Memory Technologies (CXMT) and reports that a Chinese state-backed company has started manufacturing immersion DUV lithography equipment."The market's concern lies less in CXMT's current earnings and more in its potential for accelerated capacity expansion to rival Korean companies and ⁠technology development following its IPO," said Kim Seok-hwan, a Seoul-based market analyst at Mirae Asset Securities.According to reports, South Korea's top financial regulator said it could consider imposing limits on retail investments in single-stock leveraged exchange-traded funds (ETFs) if required. Such products, introduced in May, have been cited as a source of increased market volatility.Foreign investors were net sellers of shares worth 5 trillion won (USD 3.42 billion), while retail investors purchased equities worth 4 trillion won.Market breadth remained overwhelmingly negative, with only 36 of the 917 traded stocks advancing, while 878 ended lower.The South Korean won recovered from early losses to close 0.2% stronger at 1,462.5 per US dollar on the onshore settlement platform, after having weakened as much as 0.5% to 1,472.1 earlier in the session. Traders attributed the late rebound to dollar sales by SK Hynix linked to its US share offering.
Article Summary: South Korean equities suffered their steepest one-day decline in nearly five months on Tuesday. The benchmark KOSPI slid almost 11% as a global rout in semiconductor stocks battered SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics. Investor concerns were further amplified by the blockbuster stock market debut of China's CXMT.

Article Title: US firms training AI using Chinese examples: Beijing
Article Text:
Representative image

Beijing accused US artificial intelligence firms Monday of using Chinese examples to train their models, days after Washington threatened sanctions on Chinese firms for allegedly stealing American technology."It is understood that many American artificial intelligence enterprises have distilled Chinese models during their research, development and training processes," the Chinese commerce ministry said in a statement.Distillation is a process in which an AI model is trained to mimic the output of a larger, more capable one. The method is used across the industry, but US officials say Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy proprietary American systems.The ministry said some Chinese models were released close to their US counterparts and had achieved leading capabilities in areas including front-end coding. The statement defended the use of distillation as a widely used technique across industries, while alleging that many American AI companies had distilled Chinese models. The Chinese ministry said the US accusations "lack factual basis and legal grounds, adopt double standards in practice, and constitute typical acts of artificial intelligence hegemonism"."China will take all necessary measures to firmly safeguard its interests," it added.Treasury secretary Scott Bessent last week threatened sanctions against China, amid reports the US is also weighing a ban on foreign-made open source models.
Article Summary: China accuses US of using Chinese examples to train their models. US officials say Chinese firms have deployed it at scale to illicitly copy proprietary American systems. China says the accusations "lack factual basis and legal grounds, adopt double standards in practice, and constitute typical acts of artificial intelligence hegemonism"

Article Title: US stock market today: Wall Street rallies as US-Iran tensions ease; Nasdaq rises 1%
Article Text:
Global equity markets mostly traded higher as easing tensions between the US and Iran triggered a sharp decline in oil prices.

US stock market today: US stocks opened higher on Monday while oil prices tumbled after the United States and Iran suspended military action and resumed efforts to restart negotiations aimed at ending the conflict.Early trading saw the S&P 500 rise 0.8%, recovering after two consecutive weeks of losses. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 581 points, while the Nasdaq Composite gained 1%.Financial markets welcomed the pause in fighting. US stock futures rallied early on Monday, while Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, fell 6.8% to $85.49 per barrel. US benchmark crude declined 7% to $83.06 per barrel.“Oil’s sharp retreat at the Monday open did more than knock a few dollars off the barrel. It loosened the geopolitical knot that had been tightening around equities, currencies, bonds and central banks for most of July,” Stephen Innes of SPI Asset Management said in a commentary according to an AP report.In Europe, Germany's DAX rose 1.6% to 25,497.42 in early trading, France's CAC 40 gained 0.8% to 8,436.94, and Britain's FTSE 100 advanced 0.5% to 10,784.00. Futures linked to both the S&P 500 and the Dow Jones Industrial Average were up 1%.Asian markets also ended mostly higher. Japan's Nikkei 225 added 0.5% to 64,931.19, while South Korea's Kospi climbed 1% to 6,755.75. Hong Kong's Hang Seng gained 1% to 25,207.18 and China's Shanghai Composite advanced 1.2% to 3,858.25.Australia's S&P/ASX 200 rose 1.4% to 8,894.00. Taiwan's Taiex edged down 0.1%, while India's Sensex gained 1.1%.Global equity markets mostly traded higher as easing tensions between the US and Iran triggered a sharp decline in oil prices of nearly 7%. The two sides refrained from further attacks while discussions continued on the possible revival of negotiations around an interim ceasefire.Shares of Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT jumped 466% after listing on Shanghai's technology exchange, propelling the company to the position of China's most valuable listed firm with an estimated market capitalization of 3.3 trillion yuan (nearly $490 billion).
Article Summary: US stock futures rallied early on Monday, while Brent crude, the international oil benchmark, fell 6.8% to $85.49 per barrel. The two sides refrained from further attacks while discussions continued on the possible revival of negotiations around an interim ceasefire.

Article Title: Over 500% jump! Why CXMT skyrocketed on stock market debut to become China’s most valuable listed company
Article Text:
CXMT is China's leading producer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips. (Reuters photo)

What is CXMT?

500% debut high

How does CXMT compare with its global rivals?

What are the risks?

A Chinese company has just debuted on the stock market with a 500% gain after raising a record number in Asia’s biggest public offering so far this year. Meet China's CXMT - it’s the country’s most valuable listed company - a chipmaker riding on the artificial intelligence wave.ChangXin Memory Technologies or CXMT, China's largest manufacturer of DRAM chips, raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) through Asia's biggest initial public offering this year.The stock opened at 49.50 yuan against its IPO price of 8.66 yuan, lifting the company's market capitalisation to around 3.65 trillion yuan ($539.21 billion), overtaking Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, according to a Reuters report.So what does CXMT do and why did it see such a strong stock market debut? How does CXMT rank among other major global chipmarkers?CXMT is China's leading producer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips. The chips provide temporary memory for devices such as smartphones, personal computers, servers, artificial intelligence systems and a range of other electronic products.For years, the global DRAM market has been dominated by Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix and Micron Technology.According to its IPO prospectus, CXMT is now the world's fourth-largest DRAM manufacturer, with a market share of about 7.7% in 2025.The company has benefited from the global upcycle in memory chips that began last year, driven by rising demand for AI-related applications. The resulting increase in demand has boosted both memory chip prices and spending on advanced memory technologies.According to its prospectus, first-quarter revenue surged 719% from a year earlier to 50.8 billion yuan ($7.51 billion). For the first half of this year, the company expects revenue to reach between 110 billion yuan and 120 billion yuan, almost double its full-year 2025 revenue of 61.8 billion yuan.According to the Reuters report, CXMT’s over 500% debut on the Shanghai stock market, underscores strong investor enthusiasm for a domestic semiconductor champion central to Beijing's drive for technological self-sufficiency.The surge highlights investors' willingness to assign a significant premium to one of the few pure-play semiconductor companies of its scale.The blockbuster listing has also become an important gauge of investor appetite for Chinese chipmakers at a time when global technology stocks have oscillated between AI-driven growth themes and more defensive investment strategies.Memory chips are the main component of almost every modern computing device. DRAM, in particular, is indispensable for AI servers. Training and operating artificial intelligence models require large volumes of high-speed memory.For China, CXMT plays a critical strategic role by helping reduce the country's dependence on imported semiconductors and related technologies. Beijing has been pursuing this objective for years, and the effort has gathered pace as the US and its allies have tightened export restrictions on advanced chips and semiconductor manufacturing equipment.The company's stock market debut is therefore being viewed as more than just an IPO. It serves as a test of China's ability to establish a globally competitive domestic manufacturer in a market that continues to be dominated by overseas players.Following its market debut, CXMT's valuation climbed to about $539 billion, placing it at slightly more than half the market value of Micron, despite commanding a much smaller share of the global DRAM industry.CXMT's ownership structure reflects China's state-backed approach to financing the semiconductor industry.According to its IPO prospectus, state-owned investors held a 36.29% stake in the company before the public offering. These include investment entities linked to the local governments of Hefei and Anhui, as well as China's flagship state-supported semiconductor investment vehicle, commonly known as the "Big Fund".One of the key figures behind CXMT is Zhu Yiming, the founder of GigaDevice Semiconductor, a Chinese memory chip design company best known for its NOR flash memory products used to store code in electronic devices.Company filings identify Zhu as a central force behind the establishment and growth of CXMT. He brought extensive experience from the memory chip industry during the company's formative years and later assumed the role of chairman.Although CXMT has emerged as the world's fourth-largest DRAM manufacturer, it continues to lag the industry's leading players in advanced memory technologies, particularly high-bandwidth memory (HBM) chips, which are essential for AI accelerators developed by companies such as Nvidia, according to Reuters.The HBM segment remains firmly dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix, whose leadership is underpinned by decades of manufacturing experience, advanced process technologies and long-established relationships with global customers. Micron also continues to be a major supplier of cutting-edge memory products.CXMT's competitive strength lies in different areas. The company enjoys strong government support, access to state-backed funding and rising demand from domestic customers looking to reduce reliance on overseas suppliers. These advantages could enable it to steadily increase its market share even as it remains technologically behind the industry's global leaders.In addition to the cyclical nature of the memory chip industry, CXMT faces challenges arising from US export controls, which have restricted its access to advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment supplied by companies such as ASML. Those restrictions have made it more difficult for the company to close the technology gap with its international competitors.The company also operates amid increasing geopolitical uncertainty. Last month, the US Department of Defense designated CXMT as a "Chinese Military Company". Reuters had previously reported that a US interagency committee had approved the company for inclusion on the Entity List, although that decision has not yet been implemented.According to its IPO prospectus, CXMT intends to deploy the proceeds from its public offering to expand manufacturing capacity, enhance production technology and increase investment in research and development.
Article Summary: ChangXin Memory Technologies raised 57.92 billion yuan ($8.6 billion) through Asia's biggest initial public offering this year. CXMT is China's leading producer of dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) chips. The company has benefited from the global upcycle in memory chips that began last year, driven by rising demand for AI-related applications.

Article Title: Oil prices fall 5%: Crude cools as US-Iran pause fuels hopes of diplomatic breakthrough
Article Text:
Fox News Sunday

Shipping disruptions continue

Oil prices tumbled sharply on Monday after the United States and Iran held back from launching fresh strikes over the weekend, raising hopes that diplomacy could ease tensions in the Middle East and gradually restore shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.Brent crude futures were down $4.37, or 4.52%, at $92.41 a barrel after slipping 5.05% earlier. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was also 5.23% down before trading $4.30, or 4.81%, lower at $85.01 a barrel around 7:15 am.Both benchmark contracts traded at their lowest levels in nearly a week, retreating after three consecutive weeks of gains.In early trading on Sunday, Brent crude for September delivery fell 4.9% to $92.02 a barrel after reopening, extending a 3.9% decline recorded on Friday. Benchmark US crude for September delivery dropped 5.6% to $84.34 after falling 3.1% in the previous session. Meanwhile, Brent crude for October delivery, now the most actively traded contract, declined 4.6% to $87.48.The decline came after the US and Iran refrained from carrying out military strikes in the Persian Gulf for a second straight day. The pause in hostilities followed two weeks of attacks and fuelled hopes that a diplomatic solution could help de-escalate the conflict.US ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz toldand other US media that Donald Trump had decided to pause US attacks to allow more time for diplomacy."Hopes are rising that a genuine diplomatic path may be opening," IG Markets analyst Tony Sycamore said in a note."A return to the 14-point MOU (memorandum of understanding) with a little more clarity around control of the Strait of Hormuz would be a solid starting point."Brent crude had climbed as high as $100 a barrel during the recent escalation, while it briefly touched $102 last week, its highest level since May and around $30 above the most actively traded Brent contract earlier in the month. The surge was driven by intensified fighting in the Middle East and concerns that a wider conflict would further disrupt global crude supplies.Despite the pause in attacks, shipping through key trade routes remained subdued.Shipping data from Kpler showed that fewer than 10 commodity vessels passed through the Strait of Hormuz each day over the weekend. Traffic through the Bab el-Mandeb Strait also declined on Sunday after Yemeni Houthis attacked Saudi oil installations along the Red Sea coast, although a third Chinese supertanker managed to exit through the waterway.The Strait of Hormuz has remained the focal point for oil markets since the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February. Around a fifth of the world's oil typically passes through the narrow waterway connecting the Persian Gulf to global markets, but the conflict has largely halted shipping traffic. Oil producers have sought alternative routes, though those have also come under pressure following attacks on Saudi oil tankers using the Red Sea.Although oil prices have retreated from last week's highs, uncertainty continues to linger over the conflict and its impact on energy markets. However, even with this steep rise, prices continue to be lower than the $126 per barrel mark reached earlier during the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude futures were down $4.37, or 4.52%, at $92.41 a barrel after slipping 5.05% earlier. US West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude was also 5.23% down before trading 4.81% lower at $85.01 a barrel. Both benchmark contracts traded at their lowest levels in nearly a week, retreating after three consecutive weeks of gains.

Article Title: Cheaper, open, intelligent: Chinese AI models gain ground, as they make inroads in the US
Article Text:
A booth for Chinese AI Startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 during the World AI Conference in Shanghai

HONG KONG: China has a hot new product in the United States: artificial intelligence.San Francisco-based Raffi Krikorian, the chief technology officer at Mozilla, which runs the Firefox browser, switched to Chinese AI startup Moonshot's Kimi K3 for many of his day-to-day activities within days of the new, powerful model's launch more than a week ago. "It just seems snappier," he said of K3, comparing it to the acclaimed and more expensive Claude Fable chatbot from San Francisco company Anthropic. Earlier, he had been using another high-performing Chinese model, Z.ai's GLM-5.2, for routine tasks such as managing his calendar, documents and email.Krikorian is amongst the growing number of Americans adopting Chinese AI systems, which are gaining ground around the world because they are more affordable and increasingly efficient.US companies like cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase said they're switching to Chinese AI models to help trim costs.Their popularity has frustrated some US tech giants, but short of an outright ban, they're likely to continue to appeal to independent software developers in the US and elsewhere. American-led restrictions block China from accessing some of the world's most advanced technologies including cutting-edge AI chips and US treasury secretary Scott Bessent has warned more sanctions could be coming to protect American intellectual property.Trump administration on Wednesday accused Moonshot of using "covert" but not necessarily illegal methods to build K3 off the back of Anthropic's Fable. Some US politicians and AI companies including Anthropic have accused Chinese startups of illicit "distillation" of their models to extract their technologies, a claim that Beijing rejects as "groundless."The rapid rise of cutting-edge Chinese AI models this year shows the China-US race in AI has moved on from early last year, when Chinese startup DeepSeek shook up the US technology industry and put China on the map with an AI model that performed on par with those in the US but much more cheaply.The latest AI models launched by startups Z.ai, or Zhipu, in June, and Moonshot in July are nearly as intelligent as the frontier models from OpenAI and Anthropic, experts say. Also in July, China's Alibaba previewed its Qwen3.8 Max AI model. In April, DeepSeek rolled out previews of its latest V4 model, challenging OpenAI's GPT and Google's Gemini.Based on data over the past month, the top five most popular models on OpenRouter, a platform that tracks AI models, were Chinese.Estimates from Sensor Tower, a market intelligence firm, showed China's Kimi had more than 930,000 downloads during the week after K3's July release, an increase of 200% from the week before. In the US it was downloaded around 86,000 times, a 387% jump. K3 proved so popular that Moonshot had to suspend new subscriptions as demand pushed its capacity close to its limits.
Article Summary: Mozilla's Raffi Krikorian is among the growing number of Americans adopting Chinese AI systems. US companies like cryptocurrency exchange Coinbase said they're switching to Chinese AI models to help trim costs. Some US politicians and AI companies including Anthropic have accused Chinese startups of illicit "distillation" of their models.

Article Title: Setback for Trump: US appeals court refuses to revive $100,000 H-1B visa fee
Article Text:
Trump loses bid to impose $100k fee on H-1B visa

The Trump administration suffered a setback on Friday after a US federal appeals court refused to lift a ruling that blocks the government from charging a $100,000 fee for new H-1B visas.The 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston left in place a June 8 decision that found the fee unlawful, allowing the order to remain in effect while the administration challenges it in court, reported Reuters.The case stems from a lawsuit brought by 20 Democratic attorneys general, who argued that the administration had effectively created a new tax without congressional approval. A district judge agreed, ruling that the fee exceeded the executive branch's authority.Rejecting the administration's emergency request, the three-judge appellate panel said the government had not shown it was likely to prevail in its appeal.Trump announced the steep fee increase through a presidential proclamation in September, saying it was aimed at curbing what he described as misuse of the H-1B programme by employers."The H-1B program has been deliberately exploited to replace, rather than supplement, American workers with lower-paid, lower-skilled labor," Trump had said while unveiling the measure.The H-1B programme, widely used by technology companies and other employers to hire highly skilled foreign professionals, grants 65,000 visas each year, along with an additional 20,000 visas for applicants with advanced US degrees.Before the new policy, employers generally paid between $2,000 and $5,000 in government fees to sponsor an H-1B worker. The proposed $100,000 charge applied only to new overseas applicants and did not cover foreign nationals already in the United States on student visas, who make up a large share of H-1B recipients.Court filings show that only a small number of employers have paid the fee since it was introduced.
Article Summary: The 1st US Circuit Court of Appeals in Boston left in place a June 8 decision that found the fee unlawful. The case stems from a lawsuit brought by 20 Democratic attorneys general. A district judge agreed, ruling that the fee exceeded the executive branch's authority.

Article Title: Paramount delays $81 billion Warner buyout amid legal challenge from 12 states
Article Text:
Paramount agrees to delay Warner buyout as US court reviews antitrust challenge

NEW DELHI: Paramount has agreed to postpone the completion of its proposed $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery until at least next year, giving a US federal court more time to decide a lawsuit filed by a coalition of states seeking to stop the deal.In a filing submitted on Friday, the company said it would not finalize the transaction before June 1, 2027, or until the court issues a ruling on the merits of the case, whichever comes first.The commitment follows a temporary restraining order issued earlier this week by US District Judge Araceli Martinez-Olguin, who paused the merger process after finding that the states had presented "serious questions" and a credible argument that the deal could "substantially lessen competition."Paramount described the agreement as a "significant win because the result is exactly what we have sought from the outset: a direct path to a trial based on the evidence."The media company, which was acquired by Skydance last year, said the arrangement provides the "fastest and clearest way" to demonstrate that the merger would strengthen competition and benefit the broader entertainment industry.The lawsuit, brought by 12 states led by California, argues that combining Paramount and Warner Bros.Discovery would reduce competition across Hollywood, ultimately limiting choices for consumers, including cinema audiences and cable subscribers."From the workers and artists who bring stories to life to the families who buy tickets at the box office, Paramount's illegal takeover of Warner Bros. is a bad deal for all those who count on a competitive entertainment industry," New York Attorney General Letitia James, who is among those suing to block the merger, said Friday.She called the agreement to halt the deal a "critical victory."
Article Summary: Paramount has agreed to postpone the completion of its proposed $81 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery until at least next year. A US federal court more time to decide a lawsuit filed by a coalition of states seeking to stop the deal. The company said it would not finalize the transaction before June 1, 2027.

Article Title: 'US not piggybank for Europe': Trump to impose tariffs on EU for fining Google
Article Text:
Trump to impose tariffs on EU for fining Google

US President Donald Trump on Friday threatened to impose tariffs on the European Union and launch a probe after accusing the bloc of unfairly targeting American technology companies through heavy antitrust fines.In a post on Truth Social, Trump claimed the EU had repeatedly penalised major US firms, including Google, Apple, Meta and Amazon, describing the action as discriminatory and warning that his administration would retaliate."The United States of America is not a 'PIGGYBANK' for Europe, nor will we allow it to be!" Trump wrote.The US president said Google had now been fined more than $18 billion by the European Union after being hit with another $1 billion penalty. He also alleged that Apple had been fined $15 billion, Meta $3 billion and Amazon $2.5 billion.Calling the fines "illegal and highly discriminatory", Trump announced that the US would "immediately initiate a 301 Investigation" into what he described as Europe's practice of "ROBBING" American companies and taxpayers.Section 301 of the US Trade Act allows the government to investigate and respond to foreign trade practices it considers unfair or discriminatory.Trump said the European Union would "pay a very big price" for its actions and warned that the penalties imposed on US companies would be "entirely reversed".He also signalled that his administration expected to impose "a substantial TARIFF" on the European Union "at the earliest possible moment.""The European Union is at it again and, as usual, taking direct aim at GREAT American Companies!" Trump said, adding that the alleged discriminatory treatment of US firms would not continue under his administration.He ended the post by telling followers to "Stay tuned!"
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump threatens to impose tariffs on the European Union. He accuses the bloc of unfairly targeting American technology companies through heavy antitrust fines. Trump claims the EU has repeatedly penalised major US firms, including Google, Apple, Meta and Amazon.

Article Title: US stocks today: Wall Street inches higher as crude calms down; Dow jumps over 330 points, Nasdaq trades flat
Article Text:
Oil pullback eases pressure



Tariffs, inflation and rate outlook in focus



Earnings and AI spending remain under watch



A fall in oil prices offered some relief to Wall Street on Friday, but was not enough to reverse the week's broader losses. Investors continued to weigh the impact of the Middle East conflict, fresh US tariffs and uncertainty over the Federal Reserve's next policy move.S&P 500 rose 40.73 points, or 0.55%, to 7,449.03, while Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 338.81 points, or 0.66%, to 52,050.46 around 9 pm IST. Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.94 point to 25,138.64, remaining broadly flat on the day.Despite Friday's gains, the benchmark indices were still heading towards weekly declines as investors continued to assess geopolitical tensions, tariffs and the outlook for interest rates.After climbing throughout the week, Brent crude retreated 3.5% to $97.19 a barrel. The international benchmark had climbed back above $100 on Thursday before giving up some gains. Prior to the Iran war beginning in late February, Brent had been trading at about $72 a barrel.The decline in oil prices also coincided with a modest fall in US Treasury yields. The yield on the benchmark 10-year Treasury note eased to 4.67% from 4.71% at Thursday's close, offering some support to equities.Elsewhere, European markets traded higher, while Asian markets finished the day in negative territory.Losses in a handful of heavyweight technology companies kept a lid on broader market gains.Micron Technology tumbled 6%, while Broadcom declined 2.3%. Their sharp falls weighed heavily on the Nasdaq because of their large market values and also curbed advances in the S&P 500, despite the index having more rising stocks than falling ones.Investor attention also remained fixed on the US administration's latest tariff measures, which extend to nearly all imported goods entering the country. The tariffs are paid by importers, who typically pass the higher costs on to consumers.The measures were introduced as temporary levies imposed by the president approached their Friday deadline following a Supreme Court setback for earlier tariffs.The combination of higher energy costs and fresh tariffs has added to inflation concerns, a key consideration for the Federal Reserve as it prepares for its next policy meeting later this month.Earlier expectations of an interest rate cut have faded, with markets now leaning towards another increase. According to CME FedWatch, traders expect one rate hike before the end of the year, with nearly a 36% probability that it could come at next week's meeting.Higher fuel costs are also expected to put additional strain on household budgets. AAA said the national average price of gasoline stood at $4.10 per gallon. Although that is below the levels seen during the expansion of the Iran conflict earlier this spring, it is almost a dollar higher than the price recorded at the same time last year.Beyond macroeconomic concerns, investors are also scrutinising whether companies can continue delivering earnings growth strong enough to support current valuations.American Express fell 6% even after reporting higher quarterly profit. The company maintained its full-year profit outlook while continuing to spend more heavily to retain affluent customers amid intensifying competition.Investors are also becoming more cautious about the heavy spending by AI-focused companies. Firms such as Alphabet and Nvidia continue to invest aggressively in artificial intelligence, but questions are growing over whether those investments will generate sufficient profits to support the high valuations that have driven the market's gains this year.
Article Summary: S&P 500 rose 40.73 points, or 0.55%, to 7,449.03, while Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed 338.81 points. Nasdaq Composite edged up 0.94 point to 25,138.64, remaining broadly flat on the day. European markets traded higher, while Asian markets finished the day in negative territory.

Article Title: Trump imposes new tariffs on 60 economies over forced labour concerns; India gets 10% duty - check full list

US President Donald Trump on Thursday imposed fresh tariffs on imports from 60 economies over concerns related to forced labour practices, with India among 17 economies that will face a lower 10% tariff instead of the proposed 12.5% duty.The new tariffs, imposed under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974 took effect at 12.01 am EDT on Friday, replacing the temporary 10% blanket tariff that expires at the same time.According to the Office of the US Trade Representative (USTR), goods already in transit before the deadline will remain exempt until July 28.
